Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case `testAxisPreceding()` involves an XPath expression that selects preceding nodes using the node() test. The bug report points out that the implementation of the node() test in the DOM model is incorrect because it considers only element and document nodes as matching node(), while node() should match any node type.

Specifically, the current code in `DOMNodePointer` at line 120 (likely within a method handling node tests) returns true only if the node is an element or a document. The bug report suggests that for the `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE` test, the method should always return true, matching any node type.

This is coherent with the failing test, where node() is expected to match a wider set of nodes, but because the implementation is limited to element/document nodes, the XPath does not select the correct preceding node, causing the test to fail.

Recent related issues do not contradict this and focus on different parts of the XPath implementation.

Hence, the root cause is that the method responsible for evaluating node tests in `DOMNodePointer` restricts the nodes recognized by node() to elements and document nodes, whereas it should recognize all nodes unconditionally.

This misbehavior causes XPath expressions with node() tests, like the one in the failing test, to produce incorrect results, triggering the test failure.

The fix involves modifying the logic in that method (around line 120 in `DOMNodePointer`) to return true for all node types, rather than only for elements and document nodes.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
